title: chant workspace records review output
description: What `chant workspace records review <id> --kind <kind file> --verdict <verdict> --by <principal>` prints (#2670): the record's path and id and the review entry appended, or the reason it wrote nothing. Version 1 of the write contract for records. The command writes one file or none and never commits. Readers ignore fields they do not know; a field is only ever added within a version. The error codes are a closed list, each in the one closed list of `reason-codes.ts`. Contract version 1 of this document is written by chant 0.86.0 and newer.

result.description: The record was written, or would be with --dry-run. Exit code 0.

schema.description: The `$id` of the schema the record was validated against.

file.description: The kind file, relative to the repository root, with / separators.

path.description: The record file, relative to the repository root (the working directory outside git), with / separators.

review.description: The entry appended to the record's reviews, as written.

reviewer.description: The principal given with --by, as given. chant does not check who it is; attestation of the commit that carries the review does (#2547).

note.description: The note given with --note. Absent when none was given; a dissent always has one.

on.description: The date of the verdict, in UTC.

digest.description: The digest of the record text the verdict judged: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file with LF line endings and without its reviews block (#2672), as records prints it for the record. The command changes only the reviews block, so the record keeps this digest.

session.description: The session given with --session. Absent when none was given.

dryRun.description: True when --dry-run was given and nothing was written.

warnings.description: The written record's warnings, as chant workspace records reports them. A warning never refuses a write.

text.description: With --dry-run only: the whole text of the file the command would write.

message.description: What was wrong, and what to do instead when there is something, such as writing a new record that supersedes this one.
